rationale: Built the measurement the store-failure question has been missing and asked for its formal execution. The harness drives one real raft node through three real AppendEntries RPCs on its own transport - a baseline append of entries 1 to 3 at term 1, a conflicting append of entries 2 and 3 at term 2, and a whole-log re-append of entries 1 to 3 that is what a leader sends once its rejection stair has walked back to the start of its log - with a store whose StoreLogs fails exactly once, armed only for the middle call, and it repeats the whole sequence as a control without the failure. A local construction run in the draft copy compiled and produced the intended contrast, but a local run is not evidence, so nothing here is claimed from it; the request is for the controller's clean-copy execution, and the interpretation of the receipt is left for the account that follows. No comparisons were declared: the receipt's observations carry the contrast on their own.

scope.description: Observe what a follower is left with when its AppendEntries conflict path deletes a suffix and the following store write fails, and whether a later whole-log AppendEntries is accepted, against the same sequence without the injected store failure.

experiment.prefix: Each of the two cases builds one real raft node (local id assurance-B) with an in-memory log store wrapped by a store whose StoreLogs returns an injected error once when armed, an in-memory stable store and snapshot store, a second in-memory transport registered as assurance-A connected to the node's transport, and heartbeat, election and lease timeouts of two seconds so no election interferes. The producer calls are three AppendEntries RPCs sent through the assurance-A transport into the node's own RPC handler: entries 1-3 at term 1 with previous index 0; entries 2-3 at term 2 with previous index 1, which conflicts at index 2 and makes the handler delete its suffix before storing, with the injected failure armed only in the first case; then entries 1-3 again at term 2 with previous index 0. Each case logs the handler's response fields, the node's own last log index, the wrapped store's last index and whether the store still holds index 2, right after the conflicting append and again after the whole-log append. The RPCs are supplied by the test rather than by a live leader, which is the request the follower's handler sees in either case; the supplied premise is that the conflict and the whole-log retry are what a term 2 leader produces once its rejection stair has lowered nextIndex to one.
